description: PROTOCOL_SPEC §5.16 requirements 6 and 7 (spec v1.43.0, apcore#118 decision D-72): a `pipeline:` section in the LOADED CONFIGURATION reaches the strategy the executor runs. Three fixtures already pin the builder — `pipeline_failfast_config.json`, `pipeline_hardening.json`, `pipeline_step_middleware.json` — and all three hand the section straight to `build_strategy_from_config(section, …)`. That is exactly the blind spot: the builder was never the broken part. Its first parameter is a dict the CALLER supplies, and in all three SDKs nothing extracted that dict from a `Config`, so `pipeline: remove: [acl_check]` in apcore.yaml left all eleven steps in place while every builder fixture stayed green. Every case here therefore MUST be driven through the SDK's own client/executor construction from `input.config` — a driver that calls the builder directly reproduces the defect and passes. The asymmetry is why these are MUSTs: failing to REMOVE a step is fail-safe, failing to INSERT one is not, because a declared audit, rate-limit or authorization step that never runs is invisible from inside the running system.

test_cases.description: A configuration with no `pipeline` section runs §5.6's eleven steps in order. The half that keeps requirement 6 additive for every project that configures nothing.
An empty section means the same as no section. Stated separately because implementations short-circuit it on a different branch from the absent case.
`pipeline.remove` reaches the running strategy. The step is gone and nothing else moved.

Requirement 7. Removing `acl_check` is honoured — the configuration is valid and an implementation MUST NOT reject it — and it emits a diagnostic naming the step, once per configuration load. The notice exists because of the TRANSITION: requirement 6 makes a previously ignored section take effect, so a configuration that has been carrying `remove: [acl_check]` while ACL was enforced anyway starts having ACL genuinely removed. An implementation MUST NOT reject the configuration: reaching the step assertion below is what proves it did not.

`pipeline.configure` reaches the running strategy, and §5.16 requirement 3's replace-in-place holds through the config door: the step keeps its position and there is no second entry under the same name. `raises: false` alone would also be satisfied by an implementation that accepts the field and applies none of it, so the field is read back OFF THE BUILT STEP.

The direction that is NOT fail-safe. A step declared in `pipeline.steps` is present in the running pipeline, immediately after its `after:` anchor. The driver registers a no-op step type under `input.register_step_type` first, because the type registry is an SDK-local API and the fixture cannot ship a handler.
